item.title: Badamtoli extortion goes on, two months after expose
item.description:
Illegal collections from trucks and other vehicles at Dhaka's Badamtoli fruit market continue unabated, two months after a media report exposed charges far exceeding government-approved parking fees, despite efforts by the authorities to address the irregularities.
While roadside parking has declined following police enforcement, drivers and traders say the amounts collected under the pretext of parking and selling fruit remain largely unchanged.
In its August 16 report, "Badamtoli fruit trucks caught in web of extortion", Dhaka Tribune found that truckers were charged Tk2,000-Tk5,000 through multiple collections, despite the Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority's (BIWTA) approved rate of Tk100 per truck for every three hours.
During a recent visit, the newspaper found fewer trucks parked along the road between Badamtoli and Wiseghat than before the earlier report was published.
Local drivers said police had been filing cases against illegally parked trucks after 9am, prompting many to leave early or move to designated parking areas.
BIWTA has also installed signboards displaying the approved parking rates for trucks, lorries and pickup vans. However, drivers said the notices had done little to reduce the charges.
Ahmed Ali, a pickup driver who regularly visits the market, said he pays Tk200 for parking for one to one and a half hours, while drivers unfamiliar to the collectors are charged Tk500.
"Those of us who come here every day are known to them, so they charge us less. Drivers who come after a long interval are charged Tk500," he said.
Mofij Uddin of Meem Fruits said a truck carrying oranges from Chittagong had to pay Tk3,000 to sell its goods at the market. The driver was also charged Tk500 to keep the vehicle parked after unloading.
The Tk3,000 collection alone is 20-30 times the official three-hour parking fee.
Another trader, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said they were reluctant to challenge the collections for fear of disrupting their business.
"We have come here to do business, not to get into disputes with them over the money. They are in power now, and we have to pay whatever amount they demand. There is nothing we can do," the trader said.
The parking yard remains under the alleged operational control of local BNP leader Sumon Bhuiyan, president of Dhaka South Metropolitan Sramik Dal and a prospective candidate for councillor of Ward 37.
However, the lease remains in the name of Karim Haji, whose lease was renewed. The former Awami League leader has been in hiding since August 5, 2024.
BIWTA Joint Director Md Mobarak Hossain Majumder said the authority had installed signboards to inform drivers and traders of the approved rates.
"No amount beyond the approved rate can be collected," he said, urging those charged extra to submit written complaints.
"If any trader faces such a situation, they can submit a written complaint to us. We will take action accordingly," he said.
Majumder said traders were reluctant to file written complaints, making it difficult for the authority to take action.
A BIWTA official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Sumon Bhuiyan continued to control the operation. Local traders made similar claims, while a person involved in collecting parking fees said Bhuiyan continued to pay the lease amount under a court order.
According to BIWTA, a case concerning the Badamtoli parking yard was filed on behalf of Karim Haji in 2022 and remains pending in court, preventing the authority from awarding a fresh lease.
A BIWTA source alleged that Sumon Bhuiyan was pursuing the case on Karim's behalf to retain control of the yard and prevent the authority from awarding a new annual lease. The source said Bhuiyan had an interest in maintaining the existing arrangement.
However, Dhaka Tribune could not independently verify the allegation with Karim Haji.
The August investigation also documented a Kotwali police patrol team, led by Sub-Inspector Arman, collecting Tk300 from trucks parked along the road at Wiseghat and allegedly threatening drivers with cases if they refused to pay.
Then DMP Lalbagh Division Deputy Commissioner Muhammad Talebur Rahman had ordered an investigation into the allegations against the officers.
More than two months later, however, no formal departmental disciplinary action has been taken against them, according to a source familiar with the inquiry.
The source said the officers had been verbally warned and instructed not to engage in similar activities again.
Current DMP Lalbagh Division Deputy Commissioner Md Mostak Sarkar said he was unaware of the allegations, adding that he had received no written documents concerning the matter since taking charge of the division.
Experts say failing to take disciplinary action despite evidence of misconduct can undermine accountability and allow bribery and extortion to persist within law enforcement agencies.
Kotwali police station Officer-in-Charge KM Robiul Islam told Dhaka Tribune that after seeing the report, he had issued strict instructions to all teams under his command to ensure that no police personnel became involved in similar activities.
He said police were now taking a strict stance against such misconduct.
The developments suggest that although roadside parking has improved and BIWTA has displayed the official rates, the central problem of persistent extortion remains unresolved.

item.title: Radda centre resumes services for 250 mothers, children daily
Halyards untied, flags down at Banglabandha
item.description:
Around this time last week, I was seeking refuge in the emerald embrace of northern Bangladesh, a unique geographic cusp where four South Asian nations intimately converge. Here, rushing rivers carry smooth Himalayan pebbles across the border, and hundreds of hectares of flat-land tea gardens stand as Bangladesh’s innovative answer to India’s historic highland estates just on the other side of the fence. At the Banglabandha-Fulbari border zero point, the world shrinks; standing at this vantage point, India, Nepal, and Bhutan feel well within arm's reach.
Sighting Kanchenjunga—the world’s third-highest mountain—was at the very top of my bucket list. However, a stubborn, overcast sky shattered that dream. It is a familiar gamble in these parts; as seasoned travelers say, some are lucky enough to catch the elusive mountain on their first visit, while others must return time and again. The season itself was perfect. During the crisp autumn and winter months, spanning from late October through January, Panchagarh—and specifically the Tetulia sub-district—becomes one of the rare places in Bangladesh where the snow-capped Himalayan peaks reveal themselves to the naked eye. As dawn broke last Friday, I found myself packed among several thousand hopeful souls at a riverside vantage point in Tetulia, everyone keeping their fingers crossed for a glimpse of the mountain.
It was not to be. Yet, it wasn’t the end of the world. Picturesque Panchagarh has an abundance of other quiet wonders to offer.
The codes at the top designate this spot as the beginning of the N5 National Highway, which connects Dhaka to the northern tip of Bangladesh and a segment of the Asian Highway-2 network. This landmark is situated right at the northernmost international tip of Bangladesh within the Banglabandha Land Port area in Tetulia, Panchagarh. Photo: Dhaka Tribune
Geographically, Panchagarh is wrapped on three sides by the Indian state of West Bengal. While the famous mist-shrouded hills of Darjeeling sit further north, the plains and foothills immediately adjacent to the Bangladesh border belong to the fertile Dooars-Terai tea production zone. In fact, the successful introduction of flat-land tea farming here in the late 1990s was heavily inspired by the thriving, contiguous Indian estates right across the border fence.
Unlike the traditional, rolling hill estates of Sylhet, Chittagong, or Darjeeling, Panchagarh has carved out a reputation for innovative flat-land cultivation, producing high-quality blends across expansive, level landscapes. This culturally rich northern district also boasts massive, little-explored archaeological treasures, including the ancient, preserved walled city of Bhitargarh.
When Kanchenjunga eluded me that morning, I simply refocused my lens. I turned my attention toward the endless rows of green tea leaves, the vast miles of standing golden Aman paddy, and finally, toward a deeply moving, ceremonial flag-lowering event at the Banglabandha border outpost.
A panoramic view of the flat-land tea gardens bordering the Mahananda River in Tetulia. This area is famous for tea bushes planted right up to the elevated banks of the river. The natural slope provides excellent drainage, which is ideal for the crops. Photo: Dhaka Tribune
Banglabandha is a vital port and international trade link connecting Bangladesh, India, Nepal, and Bhutan. Watching the coordinated untying of halyards by border forces wasn't a first for me, but the display of camaraderie on an international border is always a magnificent sight. The afternoon carried echoes of similar flag-down demonstrations I have admired over the years at various Indo-Bangla and Indo-Pak border crossings.
Iconic distance and directional signboard at the Banglabandha highlight the unique geographical proximity of northern Bangladesh to several major cities and neighboring South Asian countries. Once you’re here, you’re closer to all these places than the national capital Dhaka – India’s Siliguri (only 16 km away), Darjeeling (77 km), Gangtok (133 km), Bhutanese capital Thimphu (296 km) and Nepal’s Kathmandu (414 km). Photo: Dhaka Tribune
Unfortunately, I missed the full-scale theatrical display globally known as the Beating Retreat Ceremony (or Joint Retreat)—an intense, high-kicking exercise I had experienced years ago at the famous Wagah-Attari border between India and Pakistan. Unlike Wagah, where the full performance takes place daily, the joint retreat at the Banglabandha-Phulbari border by Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) and India's Border Security Force (BSF) is a biweekly affair, held only on Tuesdays and Saturdays.
Even without the dramatic, high-stepping drills that precede the crossing of the flags on those specific days, the synchronized daily joint flag-lowering ceremony I witnessed up close—standing just a few steps away from the four participating guards—was a masterclass in military precision.
Before sundown, two guards from each side stood face-to-face at the exact border line. As the trumpet sounded, the designated flag-bearers untied the interlocking ropes and began lowering the national flags in flawless, pixel-symmetric synchronization. The ritual demands absolute balance: neither flag can descend faster than the other, and they must cross paths and reach the bottom at the exact same second. Once lowered, the soldiers caught and folded the banners with meticulous care, ensuring the sacred fabric never brushed the ground.
Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel in the foreground are meticulously folding the Bangladeshi flag, while Indian Border Security Force (BSF) personnel in the background perform the exact same protocol with the Indian flag. Once carefully folded, the flags are securely stored overnight before being raised again at sunrise the following morning. Photo: Dhaka Tribune
The moment the flags were safely secured, the rigid, tense military postures dropped instantly. Commanding officers and soldiers from both the BSF and BGB stepped forward to exchange firm, formal handshakes and warm greetings, a simple yet powerful testament to bilateral peace, cooperation, and good neighborly relations.
With the folded flags tucked securely under their arms, the guards marched backward into their respective territories. At Banglabandha, I found the border forces incredibly cordial, not only to one another but also to the visiting crowds, who often grew visibly emotional and eagerly snapped photographs with the guards. This easy camaraderie speaks volumes about a deeply shared history, a connected culture, and a common language.
Beyond the border gates, Tetulia and Panchagarh possess a unique landscape that continues to fascinate travelers who make the 500-kilometer journey from Dhaka. Bordered by the scenic Mahananda and Karatoya rivers, the terrain is characterized by a distinctive sandy soil heavily embedded with smooth pebbles washed down over millennia from the Himalayan basin. The region is even home to the country's first dedicated Rocks Museum at the Panchagarh Government Women's College, which showcases ancient archaeological stone artifacts—a quiet sanctuary I had explored during a previous trip in 2024.
A close-up look at how the laborers scoop and pile the riverbed sands and stones onto their floating rings, made with bamboo and tubes, along the Mahananda River. Photo: Dhaka Tribune
This time, my journey concluded with living history. I watched locals sorting stones extracted from the rushing river currents, and observed tea tappers plucking leaves in gardens that sit side-by-side, divided only by a border line. I spent my final evening near a local hub called Borobilla, where people gather to mingle, row kayaks, and share high-spirited adda over cups of tea.
Traditional riverine stone quarrying along the Mahananda River in Tetulia. Laborers use distinctive round, tire-wrapped wicker basket rings. They dive or plunge long poles into the shallow riverbed to manually collect stones and sand drifting down from the Himalayas in India. Photo: Dhaka Tribune
At a prominent local tea house boasting dozens of varieties—ranging from heavily spiced blends to delicate black and green teas—I ordered their specialty. Rather than relying on dried, commercially processed granules, they source fresh, raw green tea leaves straight from the surrounding flat-land estates. Sipping that artisanal, vibrant kutcha pata (raw leaf) brew, I realized that even when the mountains choose to hide, the northern tip of Bangladesh never fails to deliver.
A large crowd of tourists gathered at the historic Tetulia Dak Bungalow viewpoint overlooking the Mahananda River. Perched roughly 15 to 20 meters above the riverbed, this colonial-era landmark offers a wide panorama of the river and the adjacent international border with India. Domestic travelers flock to this exact bank at dawn, hoping for a clear sky to catch a glimpse of the snow-capped peak of Mount Kanchenjunga. Photo: Dhaka Tribune

159 Dhaka-Riyadh flights cancelled, 22,721 passengers affected
item.description:
Flight cancellations between Dhaka and Riyadh have continued amid security concerns in Saudi Arabia, with 159 flights cancelled since October 10, affecting 22,721 passengers.
Kawser Mahmud, assistant director of the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh’s (CAAB) public relations department, confirmed the figures on Friday night.
Of the cancelled flights, 82 were direct services. These included 37 operated by Biman Bangladesh Airlines, 10 by US-Bangla Airlines, 20 by Saudia and 15 by Riyadh Air.
Another 77 were transit flights, including 30 operated by IndiGo, seven by SalamAir, one by EgyptAir, 14 by Emirates, nine by Qatar Airways, eight by flydubai and eight by Air India.
The CAAB official said flight cancellations would continue until the security situation improves.

item.title: Dhaka wants Thailand to buy more of its pharma, jute products to reduce trade deficit
item.description:
Bangladesh has proposed that Thailand import more pharmaceuticals and jute products from Bangladesh and reduce duties on Bangladeshi goods to improve their competitiveness in the Thai market as part of efforts to reduce the bilateral trade gap.
The Thais, during the 4th Foreign Office Consultations (FOC) held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Thailand on Friday, expressed willingness to consider the proposals and further expand bilateral trade and investment between the two countries.
The Thai delegation also requested the early initiation of discussions on a bilateral Free Trade Agreement (FTA).
The two sides reaffirmed their commitment to elevating bilateral relations through enhanced cooperation at bilateral, regional and international levels.
Foreign Secretary Asad Alam Siam led the Bangladesh delegation, while the Thai delegation was led by Permanent Secretary of the Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs Eksiri Pintaruchi.
The consultations reviewed the entire gamut of bilateral relations, including cooperation in trade and investment, connectivity, workers' migration, energy, agriculture, cultural exchanges, education and training, defence and climate change.
On connectivity, both sides welcomed the commencement of the first direct shipping service between Chittagong and Ranong ports in September 2026.
The service is expected to reduce transportation time from approximately 15 days to just four days, lowering logistics costs and boosting bilateral trade.
Bangladesh sought Thailand's technical cooperation and investment in processing Bangladeshi fruits and vegetables, as well as technology transfer to tap the global halal food market.
Under the Thailand International Cooperation Agency (TICA) programme, Bangladesh sought training for professionals in hospitality, nursing, germplasm and food processing sectors.
Thailand also stressed sharing its experience of the "One Village One Product" programme.
The two sides agreed to consider various MoUs currently under discussion, including those on rice imports and workers' migration. Both sides expressed satisfaction with the ongoing energy cooperation, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Referring to the government's national objective of generating at least 20% of electricity from renewable sources by 2030, Bangladesh sought Thailand's technical expertise and experience in converting agricultural residues and agro-industrial waste into electricity.
Looking ahead to the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Bangladesh and Thailand next year, the two sides stressed the importance of exchanges at the political level and expressed hope that visits by the heads of government next year could mark the anniversary.
They also agreed to undertake joint initiatives to promote cultural and sports exchanges.
As part of these efforts, Bangladesh offered to share its expertise in cricket and training, while Thailand offered training in Taekwondo.
On regional and multilateral cooperation, Bangladesh appreciated Thailand's continued support for its aspiration to become an Asean Sectoral Dialogue Partner and accede to the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP).
The Bangladesh delegation also sought Thailand's support in addressing the repatriation of displaced Rohingyas to Rakhine State in Myanmar.
Both sides acknowledged the growing threat of cross-border crimes, including human and arms trafficking, online scamming and narcotics trade.
In this context, they agreed to work together and consider establishing a joint committee under their respective Ministries of Home Affairs.

Bangladesh seeks stronger cultural ties with UK through creative economy
item.description:
Bangladesh is looking to strengthen cultural cooperation and people-to-people ties with the United Kingdom, with a focus on institutional partnerships, cultural exchanges and promoting its creative economy.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Friday visited the Ashmolean Museum at the University of Oxford to explore opportunities for cultural cooperation and support for Bangladeshi artists.
She visited the museum at its invitation, accompanied by Bangladesh High Commissioner to the UK Muhammad Abdul Muhith and senior officials.
During the visit, Shama toured Climate, Culture, Care, an exhibition by Bangladesh-based artist Soma Surovi Jannat, marking the first solo exhibition by an artist based in Bangladesh at a museum in the UK.
She expressed her appreciation for the intensity, depth and creativity of Jannat’s work and also visited selected collections of the museum, accompanied by its curatorial team.
The visit reflects growing recognition of Bangladesh's contemporary art and the government's efforts to use cultural diplomacy as an important instrument of foreign policy to foster mutual understanding, build bridges between societies and strengthen enduring connections between the peoples of Bangladesh and the UK, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The state minister also held discussions with Dr Mallica Kumbera Landrus, Keeper of Eastern Art and Curator at the Ashmolean Museum, on strengthening engagement between relevant authorities.
The discussions focused on institutional partnerships, cultural exchanges and initiatives to support Bangladeshi artists and develop the country's creative economy.

item.title: 4 AL & affiliate activists arrested after Dhanmondi cocktail blast
item.description:
Police have arrested four activists of the Awami League, whose activities remain banned, and its affiliate organization Jubo League after a cocktail explosion in the capital’s Dhanmondi area on Friday.
The arrestees are Md Shaminur Rahman, 53, president of the Awami League in Tejgaon Industrial Area Police Station area; Kamrun Nahar Lipi, 50, joint convener of the party in the same area; Md Nazmul Hasan, 49, an activist of the banned Jubo League; and Md Billal Hossain, 45, an Awami League activist.
According to Dhanmondi Model Police Station and Kalabagan Police Station, a group of 10-15 activists of the banned Awami League arrived in the area adjacent to the Kalabagan Krira Chakra ground on Mirpur Road around 12:05pm on Friday on seven to eight motorcycles.
They allegedly displayed banners and exploded several cocktails in an attempt to create panic and disorder.
Hearing the loud explosions, the officer-in-charge of Dhanmondi Model Police Station rushed to the spot. The miscreants also threw a cocktail targeting him, but he managed to protect himself and arrested Nazmul and Billal, police said.
Later, as the others were fleeing, Kalabagan police arrested Shaminur and Kamrun Nahar in front of Bikrampur Mistanna Bhandar, beneath the Kalabagan Bus Stand footbridge.
Police initially recovered three live cocktails from the scene. Later, acting on information provided by the arrestees, they conducted further searches and recovered 10 more cocktails, bringing the total to 13.
All 13 cocktails were subsequently safely defused by the DMP Bomb Disposal Team.
Police said legal proceedings in connection with the incident were underway.
Contacted over phone, Dhanmondi Police Station OC Imdadul Islam said the explosion occurred around 12:05pm, shortly before Juma prayers, at the intersection of Dhanmondi Road No. 8 and Road No. 10, near Kalabagan Bus Stand.
He clarified that the cocktail exploded in front of Abesh Hotel, opposite the residence of International Crimes Tribunal-2 Judge Manjurul Bashid, not directly in front of the residence.

item.title: Lightning strike kills six, injures three in Pabna
item.description:
Six people were killed and three others injured in a lightning strike while fishing in Pabna’s Gobindapur village on Friday afternoon.
The incident occurred near Sonapatila Beel in Malanchi Union of Pabna Sadar upazila.
According to locals, several people were fishing with hooks in a canal beside the river near the beel when lightning struck, killing six people on the spot and injuring three others.
Locals later rescued the injured and arranged medical treatment.
Pabna Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Sanjay Kumar Saha confirmed the incident, saying an assistant sub-inspector had been sent to the scene after police received the report.
Police are working to confirm the identities of the deceased and injured and gather further details, he said.

item.title: Dengue: 3 more die, 1,262 hospitalized in 24hrs
item.description:
Three people died of dengue in the last 24 hours till 8am on Friday, while 1,262 were hospitalized after being infected with the mosquito-borne disease during the same period.
The latest fatalities have raised the country's dengue death toll to 418 this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the newly-hospitalized dengue patients, 435 were in Dhaka Division, 75 in Mymensingh Division, 268 in Chittagong Division, 131 in Khulna Division, 112 in Rajshahi Division, 48 in Rangpur Division, 182 in Barisal Division and 11 in Sylhet Division.
According to the report, a total of 133,367 dengue patients have, so far, been hospitalized across the country this year.
So far, 126,713 dengue patients have recovered and returned home after receiving treatment in the hospitals.
A total of 102,861 people were infected with dengue, and 413 people died from the mosquito- borne disease last year.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,251 as two die in 24 hours
item.description:
Two more children died with measles symptoms in the past 24 hours, starting at 8am on Thursday.
Besides, 1,391 suspected and confirmed measles cases were reported during the same period, a press release issued by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) said here on Friday.
With two deaths, the total number of fatalities from the suspected measles reached 1,146 since March 15, 2026, the release said.
"No one died from confirmed measles in the last 24 hours," it said, adding that a total of 105 children have died from confirmed measles since March 15.
The total number of fatalities from confirmed measles and measles-like symptoms has reached 1,251 so far, since March 15.
According to the release, 1,316 suspected measles cases were reported in the last 24 hours, while the number of suspected cases stood at 227,673 from March 15 to October 30.
Since March 15, the number of confirmed measles cases was 75 in the last 24 hours, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to 23,770.
A total of 202,639 patients with suspected measles were admitted to different hospitals across the country from March 15 to October 30. A total of 194,399 patients were discharged from the hospitals during the period.

item.title: Bangladesh, Japan stress stronger economic ties, alternative financing
item.description:
Bangladesh and Japan on Friday, underscored the need to strengthen their longstanding economic relations and expand cooperation in alternative financing to accelerate infrastructure development and deepen bilateral economic partnership.
The issue came up at a bilateral meeting between Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury and his Japanese counterpart Satsuki Katayama at the Japanese Finance Minister’s office in Tokyo, according to a finance ministry media release received on Friday.
Japanese Assistant Finance Minister Mimura Atsushi also attended the meeting, which took place in a cordial atmosphere.
During the meeting, the two sides recalled the longstanding and strong economic relations between Bangladesh and Japan and held detailed discussions on ways to take their bilateral and economic partnership to a new height, said the release.
They put special emphasis on expanding economic cooperation through alternative financing mechanisms beyond foreign direct investment (FDI), alongside infrastructure development and trade expansion.
Both sides expressed their agreement to take effective initiatives to make the existing economic partnership more dynamic and explore opportunities for cooperation in new sectors. Special Assistant to the prime minister on Investment and Capital Market Affairs Tanvir Ghani and senior officials from both countries were also present at the meeting.
Japan remains one of Bangladesh’s major development partners. Japanese financing has supported several large-scale infrastructure and social development projects in Bangladesh in the past, while the two countries continue to implement important projects and sign new agreements.

item.title: CHT minister for building drug and unemployment-free Bandarban
item.description:
Chittagong Hill Tracts (CHT) Affairs Minister Sa Ching Prue on Friday expressed his determination to ensure balanced development of the CHT, create employment and build an unemployment-free Bandarban.
At the same time, he called upon leaders and activists of Jubo Dal to remain united to build a drug-free Bangladesh and a drug-free Bandarban hill district.
The minister said this while addressing a youth rally as the chief guest at the Press Club premises, held after a rally organised by the Bandarban District Jubo Dal to mark the 48th founding anniversary of Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Jubo Dal, according to a PID release.
He said the harmful impact of drugs is increasing day by day everywhere in the country and drugs have now become a national problem. Although Cox's Bazar has been identified as the main route of drugs, its serious impact is being seen in the CHT, including Naikhongchhari, Alikadam and Thanchi, he said.
Outlining the future development plans for Bandarban, the minister said balanced development of the CHT must be ensured without being driven by emotion, by keeping the bonds of amity and harmony strong.
He said extensive employment opportunities will be created in Bandarban by taking everyone along, irrespective of party and opinion.
"By adopting specific and coordinated plans, we want to build a completely unemployment-free Bandarban," he said.
Bandarban District Jubo Dal President Zahir Uddin Masum presided over the rally, while the district Jubo Dal General Secretary Md Ariful Islam Chowdhury moderated it.
A large number of leaders and activists of the Bandarban unit of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and its various associate organisations were present at the programme.

item.title: Tuku: Govt working to ensure healthcare services for disadvantaged people
item.description:
State Minister for Fisheries and Livestock Sultan Salahuddin Tuku has said the government is prioritising efforts to ensure healthcare assistance and development programmes reach disadvantaged people at the grassroots level.
He said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has placed particular emphasis on supporting underprivileged people, especially those suffering from cancer, kidney disease and other critical illnesses, by providing financial assistance for their treatment.
Tuku made the remarks on Friday afternoon while distributing cheques among poor patients suffering from cancer, kidney disease and other complex illnesses at the Tangail Sadar Upazila Parishad building.
He said anyone suffering from a serious illness who had not yet received medical assistance could apply for support, pledging to take all possible steps to help them. “The programme will continue. We are committed to the people and will continue working for their welfare,” he said.
The state minister added that the scope of government assistance had expanded across various sectors since the BNP assumed office. Initiatives include family cards, farmer cards and allowances for imams and muezzins, alongside development activities across the country.
He said the government was taking all possible measures to ensure that public services and assistance reached people at the grassroots level.
At the programme, six patients each received Tk100,000, bringing the total amount distributed to Tk600,000.
Tangail Sadar Upazila Nirbahi Officer Shaheen Mia chaired the event. Among those present were former Tangail district BNP general secretary Mahmudul Haque Sanu, Tangail Sadar Thana BNP President Azgar Ali, former district BNP organising secretaries Ashraf Paheli and Shafiqul Rahman Shafik, and Tangail district Jubo Dal Convener Khandaker Rashedul Alam Rashed.
Union parishad chairmen, leaders and activists of the BNP and its affiliated organisations, and local dignitaries also attended.
After the cheque distribution, Tuku inaugurated a visitors' room at his office as part of efforts to improve public access to services and make government activities more accessible.

item.title: Biman forms probe body over technical glitch on PM's flight
item.description:
Biman Bangladesh Airlines has formed an investigation committee to determine the cause of a technical malfunction that delayed a flight carrying Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and his entourage in Japan.
Shahnur Ahmed, general manager of Biman's public relations department, confirmed the development to Dhaka Tribune on Friday.
He said the airline had formed an internal committee under its standard procedure for investigating such incidents and instructed it to submit its findings promptly.
The committee will be headed by Biman's Chief of Planning and Scheduling. Its members include the chief engineer (Engineering Production), deputy chief (Flight Safety) and manager (Legal Affairs), who will serve as member secretary.
The committee has been tasked with identifying the cause and nature of the malfunction, reviewing the measures taken to ensure the aircraft's airworthiness, and assessing the impact on flight schedules, passengers and the airline's reputation.
It will submit its report to Biman's managing director and chief executive officer.
Flight BG377, carrying the prime minister and his entourage, departed Narita International Airport in Japan five and a half hours behind schedule due to the technical glitch.
Biman's engineering team and Japanese technicians completed the repairs. The aircraft was pushed back at 7:43pm Bangladesh time and departed for Dhaka at 7:55pm.

PM returns home after four-day Japan visit
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman returned home early on Friday wrapping up his four-day official visit to Japan aimed at strengthening bilateral ties, attracting investment and expanding trade and economic cooperation between the two countries.
“A Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight carrying the prime minister, his wife Dr Zubaida Rahman and members of his entourage landed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at 2:48am,” said Prime Minister’s Deputy Press Secretary Shahadat Shadhin.
Earlier, the flight departed Narita International Airport in Tokyo at 10:55pm local time on October 29, he added.
At the invitation of Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, Tarique Rahman's visit featured high-level bilateral talks, the signing of cooperation agreements, discussions with Japanese business leaders on investment opportunities in Bangladesh, and visits to major industrial and energy facilities.
During the bilateral summit at the Japanese Prime Minister's Office on October 27, Tarique Rahman and Takaichi discussed strengthening the longstanding partnership between the two countries, with particular emphasis on trade, investment, energy security, infrastructure, technology, space research and regional and international affairs.
The two leaders also discussed a proposed private investment of one trillion Japanese yen (US$6.3 billion) in Bangladesh's energy, infrastructure and information and communication technology (ICT) sectors.
They discussed sending a Japanese team to Bangladesh to expedite progress on the investment plan.
Bangladesh secured pledges for two yen-loan projects worth a combined 46.56 billion yen, equivalent to approximately $295.5 million and signed six bilateral cooperation instruments during the visit.
The instruments included a grant agreement of up to 2.12 billion yen ($13.44 million) for a patrol vessel to strengthen Bangladesh's coastal security capabilities.
The two countries also signed memorandums of cooperation on improving the business environment, agriculture, the Employment for Skill Development Programme, and fisheries and livestock, alongside a letter of intent on climate change cooperation.
The two loan projects will support improvement of the investment environment in Bangladesh and the second phase of the Upazila Governance and Development Project.
Beyond the government-level agreements, 17 memorandums of understanding (MoUs) were signed between private-sector entities at the Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO), according to State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir.
On October 28, the prime minister addressed the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Forum Dialogue at JETRO headquarters in Tokyo, inviting Japanese companies to invest in five priority areas: automotive manufacturing, energy, technology and space, high-speed rail and logistics, and agro-processing.
He pledged government support and reforms to improve the business environment.
During the visit, Tarique Rahman also met Japanese political leaders, development partners and business executives, including former prime minister Taro Aso, Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) President Dr Akihiko Tanaka, Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC) Governor Kazuhiko Amakawa and JETRO President Susumu Kataoka.
In meetings with representatives of major Japanese companies, including apparel giant Uniqlo, Mitsui & Co., Sumitomo Corporation and JERA, he explored opportunities to expand investment, establish factories, create jobs, facilitate technology transfer and develop skills.
The prime minister visited JERA's liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal and power plant in Futtsu and the Nittsu Logistics Hub in Ichikawa on October 27 to observe Japan's energy and logistics facilities.
On Thursday, he travelled to Nagoya and visited Toyota Motor Corporation's Motomachi factory and the Toyota Commemorative Museum of Industry and Technology, where he observed Japan's automotive manufacturing capabilities.
The visit comes as Bangladesh and Japan seek to expand economic engagement following the signing of their first-ever Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) in February 2026, providing a new framework for strengthening trade and commercial ties.
Japan has long been one of Bangladesh's major development partners, supporting key infrastructure projects, including Dhaka metro rail, the third terminal of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport and Matarbari deep-sea port.

item.title: Bangladesh wins three more years before LDC graduation
item.description:
Bangladesh has secured three more years to prepare for its graduation from the United Nations’ least developed country (LDC) category, pushing the deadline from November 24, 2026, to November 24, 2029, and giving the country crucial time to protect its export competitiveness and address longstanding economic weaknesses.
The UN General Assembly approved the extension on Thursday following a proposal introduced by Uruguay on behalf of Bangladesh and Nepal, with the backing of the Group of 77 and China.
The decision followed a favourable assessment by the UN Committee for Development Policy (CDP) and a recommendation from the UN Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC).
Bangladesh had sought the extension amid mounting economic pressures, including global trade uncertainty, energy supply disruptions, sluggish investment and persistent weaknesses in its banking and industrial sectors.
Although Bangladesh has already met all three UN criteria for LDC graduation, the government argued that additional preparation time was necessary to manage the transition without exposing its export industries to sudden competitive disadvantages.
The extended period will allow Bangladesh to pursue new trade agreements, strengthen industrial productivity, diversify exports and undertake reforms aimed at improving its competitiveness after graduation.
The most immediate concern is the future of Bangladesh’s export trade, particularly the ready-made garment industry, which accounts for the overwhelming majority of the country’s merchandise export earnings.
As an LDC, Bangladesh enjoys duty-free and quota-free access to several international markets, including the European Union under its Everything But Arms arrangement.
Graduation would begin the process of withdrawing some of these benefits, although the timing would vary according to the rules of individual trading partners.
Under the EU’s current arrangements, graduating countries generally receive a three-year transition period before losing LDC-specific preferences.
Without an alternative trade arrangement, Bangladeshi garment exporters could eventually face tariffs of around 12% in the EU market, weakening their competitiveness against countries enjoying preferential access.
A three-year delay in graduation could therefore provide additional time to secure trade agreements and prepare businesses for tougher competition.
However, extending LDC status would not guarantee that every existing benefit remains unchanged, as trade preferences and financing arrangements are governed by separate rules.
Bangladesh formally requested the extension in February 2026, citing the lingering effects of the pandemic, geopolitical conflicts, international trade uncertainty and pressure on energy supplies.
The CDP subsequently concluded that an extension would be appropriate, provided Bangladesh made substantial progress in addressing its structural vulnerabilities.
In July, ECOSOC recommended that the General Assembly consider the request before the existing graduation deadline.
The UN assessment identified financial-sector instability, weak domestic revenue mobilisation, limited export diversification and inadequate productive capacity among the areas requiring urgent attention.
These problems have persisted despite Bangladesh’s progress in meeting the economic and social indicators for graduation.
The additional period, if approved, would give policymakers more time to strengthen the banking system, increase tax revenue, improve infrastructure and reduce the cost of doing business.
The government has been pursuing bilateral and regional trade arrangements to protect market access after graduation.
Commerce, Industries and Textiles and Jute Minister Khandaker Abdul Muktadir has said the government aims to conclude comprehensive economic partnership or free trade agreements with eight to ten countries during 2026–27.
Bangladesh is also exploring closer trade arrangements with the European Union and opportunities under the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership.
The government has identified lengthy licensing procedures, regulatory delays and unreliable energy supplies as obstacles to investment and industrial expansion.
Proposed measures include digitalising business registration, streamlining licensing and improving coordination among regulatory agencies.
But trade agreements alone will not resolve the country’s competitiveness challenges. Exporters will also need to improve productivity, diversify products and comply with international labour, environmental and rules-of-origin requirements.
The UN’s assessments have made clear that any additional preparation period must be used to accelerate reforms rather than postpone difficult decisions.
Bangladesh would be expected to make measurable progress under its national smooth transition strategy, including financial-sector reform, revenue mobilisation and export diversification.
The government has maintained that it remains committed to graduating from LDC status and views the extension as a means of ensuring a sustainable transition.
For Bangladesh’s exporters, the stakes are substantial. An additional three years could create room to negotiate better market access and improve industrial capacity.
But the longer-term outcome will depend on whether that time produces meaningful reforms before the country eventually loses its LDC-specific advantages.

item.title: Irene Khan: Women’s participation key to sustainable peace and security
item.description:
Bangladesh's Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Irene Zubaida Khan, has called for meaningful women's participation in peace processes and decision-making, emphasising that grassroots initiatives are vital to preventing violence and building lasting peace.
Speaking at the UN Security Council's open debate on Women, Peace and Security (WPS) recently, she recalled Bangladesh's role as a key co-sponsor of Security Council Resolution 1325 and reaffirmed the country's commitment to the WPS agenda, according to the Bangladesh mission.
Irene Khan highlighted Bangladesh's National Action Plan on WPS, introduced six years ago.
After completing its first phase, Bangladesh is now implementing the second phase, with consultations involving stakeholders, particularly civil society and women's groups, remaining a key feature of the process.
The Bangladesh permanent representative underscored the importance of training and sensitising girls and young women on violence prevention and supporting their active participation in community-level mediation.
She stressed that grassroots efforts can prevent disputes from escalating into wider conflicts, noting that Bangladesh is prioritising these initiatives through government and NGO programmes.
Irene Khan also called for greater investment in women's organisations and human rights defenders, protection for women in conflict-affected settings, and predictable, sustained financing for peace operations and vulnerable communities.
Emphasising a gender-centred approach to security, she stressed that women must have a meaningful voice in peace negotiations, political leadership and decision-making.
The Bangladesh permanent representative urged the international community to translate WPS commitments into concrete action to advance inclusive sustainable peace.

item.title: Fishermen in Chandpur return to rivers as hilsa fishing ban ends
item.description:
Around 42,000 fishermen in Chandpur resumed ilish fishing in the Meghna and Padma rivers early Friday after a 22-day ban imposed by the government to protect mother ilish during the breeding season.
The ban on catching, selling and transporting ilish officially ended at 11:59pm on Thursday, allowing the fishermen to return to fishing after weeks of hardship.
District Fisheries Officer Fakhrul Islam said authorities maintained strict monitoring throughout the 22-day ban.
He said extensive drives were conducted across the rivers throughout the 22-day ban period to safeguard mother ilish.
Joint forces comprising the district and upazila administrations, the Fisheries Department, river police, the Bangladesh Coast Guard and the district task force patrolled the 70-kilometre sanctuary area day and night.
During this period, 238 operations and 72 mobile court drives were conducted in the sanctuaries.
These efforts resulted in the seizure of approximately 2.75 tonnes of mother ilish (egg-bearing ilish), as well as fishing nets worth Tk 2.71 crore, which were later destroyed.
A total of 161 cases were filed, and mobile courts collected approximately Tk 4 crore in fines for violations of the government ban.
Furthermore, 183 fishermen from Chandpur Sadar, Matlab Uttar and Haimchar were detained for catching mother ilish in the Padma-Meghna sanctuaries during this period. They were subsequently sentenced to imprisonment and/or fined.
To support those affected by the ban, the government distributed 25 kg of rice to each unemployed fisherman as temporary relief.
Many fishermen, however, voiced concerns that this assistance was insufficient.
Talking to UNB on Thursday, fishermen from Saformali, Lalpur, Anandabazar, Baharia, Dokanghar, Ramdasdi and Harina Ferry Ghat said rice alone was not enough to sustain their families.
They also demanded cash assistance alongside rice from the government.
Expressing their frustration, the fishermen said they were forced to take on debt just to manage their daily living expenses and were now deeply worried about how they will repay these loans.
"If at least Tk 3,000 per person were allocated, it would have provided some relief," they said.
The government imposed the 22-day fishing ban in the Padma-Meghna rivers in Chandpur from October 8 to protect mother ilish and boost future production of the country's national fish.

Section 144 imposed in Inani as gas fire burns for fourth day
item.description:
A fire fuelled by natural gas escaping from underground has continued for four days in Inani, Ukhiya, Cox's Bazar, prompting the local administration to impose Section 144 around the site to ensure public safety.
People have been barred from entering or staying within a 200-metre radius of the gas emission site.
The incident began on Tuesday, when a local resident, Abdullah, arranged for drilling work to install a tube well in his yard. Gas started escaping through the borehole, followed by flames.
As a precaution, families living near the site have been moved to safer locations. Authorities have also fenced off the area within a 200-metre radius with barbed wire and placed red flags to warn people.
Electricity supply in the area was initially suspended for safety reasons but was later restored through an alternative arrangement.
The incident has drawn crowds of curious onlookers, including tourists visiting Marine Drive and people travelling from distant areas.
SM Nafefun Arham, party chief of a geological survey team that visited the site, said the gas should be allowed to escape naturally for now.
He said the fire must not be extinguished and the gas flow must not be obstructed, as doing so could cause gas to accumulate underground and create high pressure. This could lead to an explosion, potentially putting a much wider area at risk.
He said the gas flow should initially be monitored for 15 days. If the flow gradually decreases, it may eventually stop on its own. If it does not, experts will be consulted on measures to control it.
Ukhiya Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Panna Akter said Section 144 had been imposed in the interest of public safety, prohibiting entry and movement within 200 metres of the fire's source.
She said people had also been instructed not to light fires, smoke or use matches or lighters in the area. The restrictions will remain in place until further notice.

item.title: Rafi sets four national records in two days at National Swimming
item.description:
Bangladesh Navy swimmer Samiul Islam Rafi made a sensational start to the 35th National Swimming, Diving and Water Polo Championship, setting four new national records in just two days at the Syed Nazrul Islam National Swimming Complex in Mirpur, Dhaka.
After breaking the men's 50m backstroke record on the opening day, Rafi continued his record-breaking run on the second day, setting three more national marks, including individual records in the men's 50m butterfly and 100m freestyle.
The Navy swimmer clocked 25.81 seconds in the men's 50m backstroke to better his previous national record of 26.05 seconds, set in 2025.
He then clocked 24.98 seconds in the men's 50m butterfly, improving his previous record of 25.15 seconds, before setting another national record in the men's 100m freestyle with a time of 51.80 seconds, bettering the previous mark of 52.42 seconds.
Rafi completed his four-record haul by helping Bangladesh Navy's mixed 4x100m medley relay team, alongside Mohammad Islam, Mukta Khatun and Fatiha Mahtab Maisha, clock 4:20.36 to improve the Navy's previous record of 4:24.55.
Rafi has also won four gold medals so far in the competition, capping an impressive individual performance.
His achievements followed an impressive outing at the 2026 Thailand Age Group Swimming Championships (25m) – Open/Senior Group G, where he won two gold and one bronze medal.
The second day of the national championship also witnessed several other record-breaking performances. A total of 14 new national records were established across swimming and diving events during the first two days, with six set on the opening day and eight on the second.
Organised by the Bangladesh Swimming Federation with sponsorship from Max Group, the October 28-31 championship features around 470 male and 102 female swimmers representing approximately 79 teams.

item.title: Advantage Australia as WTC series hangs in the balance
item.description:
Nathan Lyon ended South Africa captain Temba Bavuma’s resistance in the middle as Australia closed Day 3 of the third ICC World Test Championship Test in an advantageous position.
With a 40-run lead in the second innings, the Proteas are four wickets down in the second innings at the score of 140 and with Matthew Breetzke (19*) and Ryan Rickelton (8*) at the crease.
Australia centurion Josh Inglis believes his side is on top, with Nathan Lyon's late wicket of South Africa skipper Temba Bavuma a key moment in the game.
"I think we controlled the tempo really well in that last session," Inglis said.
"Although they were playing well, they weren't really getting away from us. I thought Gaz (Lyon) bowled brilliantly and looked threatening the whole time.
"When you work for a couple of hours and get the rewards right at the end, it's really satisfying,"
South Africa spinner Simon Harmer thinks there is still plenty of cricket left in the series decider and his spin may still have a big say across the final two days of play.
"If you look at how the wicket changed from this morning to this evening, it's been quite a dramatic change," Harmer noted.
"I think Mitchell Starc does a pretty good job of churning up the wicket (with footmarks).
"So yeah, I definitely think that spin is probably going to come into it a lot more than it has in the first two-and-a-half days."
The hosts had mounted an impressive display earlier on Day 3, restricting Australia to 429 after they began the day’s play with six wickets in hand and 330 runs on the board.
Inglis went on to complete an impressive century while Alex Carey also compiled 80 runs. For the home side, Marco Jansen and Harmer split seven wickets between them.
While Harmer finished with bowling figures of 4/104, Jansen continued his impressive run in the series with 3/60.
The performance comes on the back of the left-arm quick rising to the top of the ICC Men’s Test Bowling Rankings as well as the Test All-Rounders Rankings.
Trailing by 100 runs in the first innings, the Proteas were put on the back foot early on the innings as Mitchell Starc got rid of Aiden Markram in the third over.
A second wicket followed soon as Josh Hazlewood removed David Bedingham from the equation.
It was from here that South Africa’s highest run-getter in the first innings, Marques Ackerman and Bavuma, added crucial runs on the board.
The pair added 64 runs for the third wicket partnership as Ackerman scored his second half-century of the Test.
Starc however, got Australia right back into the game, snapping Ackerman. A final blow to the visitors was dealt by Lyon in the penultimate over as Bavuma returned to the dressing room.
Series schedule
First Test: 9-13 October, Durban (Australia won by 214 runs)
Second Test: 18-22 October, Gqeberha (South Africa won by an innings and 31 runs)
Third Test: 27-31 October, Cape Town

item.title: Technical glitch fixed; Biman flight carrying PM expected to leave Tokyo for Dhaka shortly
item.description:
The technical glitch on the Biman Bangladesh Airlines aircraft that delayed Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s flight to Dhaka from Tokyo was fixed on Thursday night, and the flight is expected to leave Narita International Airport shortly.
Captain Md Imamul Islam announced around 9:50pm local time that the problem was resolved and that passengers would start boarding the aircraft again soon.
The Biman flight was scheduled to leave Tokyo at 6pm local time.
The aircraft left its terminal around 6:18pm and moved to the runway for takeoff.
However, it stopped before taking off, and about 15 minutes later, the captain announced that the flight could not proceed due to a technical problem.
He said two engineers were working to resolve the issue. The aircraft was later taken back to the tarmac, and all passengers disembarked.
Around 8pm local time, the captain announced that it would take another two and a half hours to fix the problem.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, his wife Dr Zubaida Rahman and other members of his entourage were on board the aircraft.
The flight was originally scheduled to arrive at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at 10:35pm Bangladesh time.
Tarique arrived in Japan on Monday on a four-day state visit at the invitation of Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.

item.title: Two shot dead in Pabna
item.description:
Two men, including a leader of the banned Sramik League, were shot dead by unidentified assailants at Pushpapara cattle market in Pabna’s Ataikula upazila on Thursday evening.
The deceased were identified as Abdus Salam, 56, convener of the banned Pabna Sadar upazila unit of Sramik League and lessee of the cattle market, and his nephew Ripon Hossain, 35, president of the Ataikula union unit of Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal.
The shooting took place at around 6:30pm while the two were inside their office at the market, according to eyewitnesses. A group of assailants arrived and opened fire indiscriminately at them.
Local residents rescued the two men and took them to Pabna General Hospital, where doctors declared them dead.
Ataikula police station Officer-in-Charge Pradip Kumar confirmed the incident. He said police had been sent to the scene and arrangements were being made for autopsies. Several police teams were investigating the killings, he added.
Pabna Superintendent of Police Abu Ashraf said investigators were examining two possible motives: a dispute over the cattle market lease and rivalry involving extremist groups.
Salam was a resident of Dharmagram village in Ataikula union. According to Pradip Kumar, general secretary of the banned Pabna district Sramik League, Salam had been the convener of the organization’s Sadar upazila unit. After the political changeover on August 5, 2024, he had posted photographs with leaders of other political parties on social media, Pradip said.
Abdul Gafur, president of the Pabna district unit of Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal, confirmed that Ripon was president of the organization’s Ataikula union unit.

item.title: Home minister: Cause of ex-BAF officer’s death to be known after autopsy
item.description:
The cause of death of retired Bangladesh Air Force (BAF) Flight Lieutenant Tahsif Souri will be known after the completion of the preliminary investigation and autopsy, said Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Thursday.
“Once we receive the post-mortem report and examine all relevant aspects, we will be able to provide further details,” he told reporters after attending a program at the parade ground of Bangladesh Police Academy at Sarda in Rajshahi.
It is not possible to confirm the cause of death before the investigation and autopsy, he said.
Referring to the law and order situation, the minister said the government is successfully identifying and arresting suspects, conducting investigations and ensuring trials after crimes are committed.
However, he acknowledged that there might be exceptions in a few cases.
The minister also claimed that since the BNP assumed office, there have been no extrajudicial killings by law enforcement agencies, bomb attacks or deaths in custody.
Earlier, river police have recovered the body of a former Bangladesh Air Force officer, Tahsif Souri, from the Turag River in Dhaka.
Inspector Firoz Uddin of the River Police’s Tongi outpost told the media on Thursday that they received information through the national emergency service 999 and recovered the floating body from the Rajabari Ghat area of the river around 4:30pm on Wednesday.
“We found a mobile phone with him and identified him through the phone,” he said.
Shahinur Zaman, duty officer at Uttarkhan Police Station, said on Thursday morning that the Tongi River Police outpost recovered the body from the Turag River on Wednesday afternoon.
As the matter fell under the jurisdiction of the River Police, its members went to the spot and took the body away.
Inspector Firoz Uddin said there were no visible injury marks on the body.
The body of Tahsif was sent to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital for an autopsy to determine the cause of death.
According to the River Police’s preliminary report, Souri was wearing white pyjamas and a black shirt.
A wristwatch was found on his hand, while an iPhone was found in his pocket.
Souri reportedly recorded the video that circulated on August 5, 2024, showing then Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina leaving the country by an aircraft from Kurmitola Airport.

item.title: Swapan: Misinterpretation of religion, patriarchal mindsets hinder women's empowerment
item.description:
Misinterpretation of religion and patriarchal attitudes remain major challenges to gender equality and women's empowerment in Bangladesh, Prime Minister's Political Adviser Zahir Uddin Swapan said on Thursday.
“Misinterpretation of religion and patriarchal attitudes remain major challenges to achieving gender equality and ensuring women’s empowerment in Bangladesh. These challenges must be addressed if we are to build an equitable, inclusive and developed Bangladesh. Alongside reducing existing inequalities between women and men, it is essential to ensure equal opportunities for women in education, employment, leadership and decision-making,” he said.
Swapan made the remarks while speaking as the chief guest at the 'IDG Carnival 2026', organised by Save the Children in Bangladesh at a hotel in the capital to mark the International Day of the Girl.
He stressed the need to address these challenges and ensure equal opportunities for women in education, employment, leadership and decision-making to build an equitable, inclusive and developed Bangladesh.
Held under the theme "Rooted in Every Region, Advancing Every Adolescent Girl", the event brought together policymakers, development partners, youth representatives and other stakeholders to promote the rights, leadership and meaningful participation of girls and adolescent girls in society.
The prime minister's adviser said the government placed particular importance on gender equality and women's empowerment as part of its vision for building the Bangladesh of the future.
However, achieving these goals required effective contributions from both the government and development partners, he said.
"Save the Children's experience, support and partnerships can make an important contribution in this regard," Swapan said, expressing hope that the organisation would continue working with the government to advance women's rights, eliminate discrimination and build a more equitable society.
Dr Md Saimum Parvez, special assistant to the prime minister on environment, forest and climate change, attended the event as the guest of honour.
Members of Parliament Helen Zerin Khan, Mahmuda Habiba and Mansura Akter attended as special guests, while Dr Eliza Azei, head of the Adolescents and Youth Programme at UNFPA Bangladesh, was also present.
Discussions at the carnival highlighted the need to remove barriers that prevent girls and adolescent girls from accessing education, employment, leadership opportunities, entrepreneurship and decision-making processes.
The government places particular importance on gender equality and women’s empowerment as part of its vision for building the Bangladesh of the future, said the PM's Adviser.
However, achieving this goal requires effective contributions not only from the government but also from development partners.
The event highlighted the importance of creating opportunities for girls and adolescent girls to realise their potential, develop leadership skills and participate actively in decision-making processes.

Participants expressed their expectation that creating equal opportunities for adolescent girls, amplifying their voices and increasing their participation in policymaking and decision-making processes will contribute to building a more equitable and inclusive society.

item.title: Shama outlines Bangladesh’s foreign policy vision at Chatham House
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Thursday outlined the government’s strategic vision for strengthening social resilience and promoting sustainable and inclusive growth.
The state minister, while addressing a roundtable discussion hosted by Chatham House, one of the world’s foremost international affairs think tanks, in London also outlined the government’s strategic vision for fostering constructive engagement and friendly relations with all countries, guided by the principles of mutual respect and dignity.
The session brought together scholars, academics and experts from Chatham House and other leading UK research and academic institutions.
The discussion covered a wide range of issues, including Bangladesh’s development priorities, economic diplomacy, business and investment, human rights, youth empowerment, food security, technology-driven economic growth and the creative economy.
Climate resilience, climate finance and priorities ahead of COP31, as well as Bangladesh’s foreign policy approach and engagement with international partners, were also among the key themes.
The state minister elaborated on the Government’s major initiatives, key priorities and foreign policy objectives, underscoring their alignment with the electoral manifesto.
High Commissioner of Bangladesh to the United Kingdom Muhammad Abdul Muhith and senior officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Bangladesh High Commission in London were also present.
The discussion was held under the Chatham House Rule, facilitating an open exchange of perspectives.

item.title: EC secretary: EC satisfied with peaceful Thakurgaon-1 by-election
item.description:
Election Commission (EC) Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed on Thursday expressed satisfaction over the peaceful completion of the parliamentary by-election to the Thakurgaon-1 constituency, as no reports of untoward incidents had been received throughout the day.
“We have completed a good election in a peaceful environment with everyone's cooperation,” he said at a post-balloting briefing at the Election Commission Building in the city’s Agargaon area in the afternoon.
The EC secretary said the commission had not received any reports of untoward incidents from anywhere since the morning.
“I believe you also have no such information that could make us concerned,” he said, thanking everyone for their cooperation in holding the election peacefully.
In response to a question about whether the EC was satisfied with the polls, Akhtar Ahmed said: “Surely satisfied. Is there any reason not to be satisfied?”
Asked whether the EC had passed the test set by the 11-party alliance, which had described the by-election as a test for the commission before deciding whether to participate in the upcoming local government elections, he said, “If we had not passed, would we be briefing you?”
He said the voting in the by-election began at 8am and ended at 4pm. All polling stations completed voting, and no voters were waiting to cast their ballots at the end of polling.
The EC secretary said: “Voters exercised their franchise in a festive atmosphere.“
The Thakurgaon-1 constituency, covering Thakurgaon Sadar, Ruhia and Bhulli upazila, fell vacant after Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir assumed office as president.
BNP-nominated candidate Mirza Faisal Amin, who is the younger brother of President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, and Jamaat-e-Islami candidate Delwar Hossain are considered frontrunners in the by-election.
The Thakurgaon-1 constituency has a total of 185 polling stations. Of them, 113 are in Thakurgaon Sadar upazila, 33 in the newly formed Ruhia upazila and 39 in Bhulli upazila.
The constituency has 515,853 voters, including 257,219 men, 258,630 women and four third-gender voters.

item.title: Thakurgaon-1 by-election ends, vote counting begins
item.description:
Polling in the Thakurgaon-1 by-election concluded without any reported violence or disorder on Thursday, with voting ending at around 4:30pm after starting at 8am.
The constituency covers Thakurgaon Sadar, Ruhia and Bhulli. Vote counting began immediately after polling ended.
Voter turnout was relatively low in the morning but increased toward noon, according to observations at several polling centers across the constituency. Reports from different centers indicated that around 50-60% of votes had been cast by noon.
At Krishnapur Government Primary School polling center in Ward 8 of Rahimnagar Union, presiding officer Saiful Islam said around 40% of votes had been cast by 12:30pm.
Voters Farazul Islam of Paikpara village and Farhad Hossain of Prostampur village said they had cast their ballots in a peaceful environment and described voter turnout as good.
At Polling Centre No 112 at Raipur Government Primary School in Election Area 3 of Thakurgaon Sadar upazila, around 55% of votes had been cast by 1:30pm.
Promila, a voter from the Raipur area, said she had come to vote with her husband, while her son and daughter-in-law had voted in the morning. Another voter from the same area, Madhai Chandra, also arrived with his wife to cast his ballot.
However, Abdul Latif, a voter from Gobindanagar, said he faced difficulties at Thakurgaon Government Polytechnic Institute while helping his ailing wife, Sharifa Begum, cast her vote.
He said he struggled to take her to the second floor and argued that polling booths for sick voters and people with mobility difficulties should not have been placed there.
A mobile court fined Abdul Karim, president of the Jamaat-e-Islami Ward 1 unit in Jagannathpur Union of Thakurgaon Sadar upazila, Tk5,000 for allegedly distributing leaflets at JP School polling center in the Jagannathpur area around noon.
He faces 1 month of simple imprisonment if he fails to pay the fine.
Meanwhile, law enforcement agencies detained 3 alleged fake voters at Danarhat Ansaria Fazil Madrasa polling center in Thakurgaon Sadar around noon on Thursday.
The detainees were identified as Himel and Siam, second-year students of the Alim program, and Minhaj, a first-year Alim student at the madrasa.
A total of 516,138 voters are eligible to vote in the by-election, which is being held at 185 polling centers across Thakurgaon Sadar, Ruhia and Bhulli, with 989 polling booths.
Five candidates are contesting the seat: BNP's Mirza Faisal Amin; Md Delawar Hossain, backed by the 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami; Hafez Dr Md Khademul Islam of Islami Andolan Bangladesh; Md Abdul Alim Nizami of Bangladesh Khelafat Andolan; and Husain Muhammad Omar Faruk of Bangladesh Congress.
Extensive security measures have been deployed by law enforcement agencies and the administration. Around 5,300 law enforcement personnel are on duty, and closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras have been installed at all polling centers.
BNP candidate Mirza Faisal Amin said voting was taking place in a festive atmosphere.
“Undoubtedly, voting is taking place in a festive atmosphere. Every voter is my voter. All voters in this area want to cast their votes peacefully. Despite this being a by-election, a large turnout has been observed. I still believe that the voters' opinions are final,” he said.
Md Delawar Hossain, the candidate backed by the 11-party alliance, said the election's credibility depended on the government and those responsible for conducting it, as the vote was being held under a party-led government.
“Since this election is being held under a party-led government, it depends entirely on the government and those responsible for conducting the election. If the government, administration and election officials act sincerely, they can deliver a free and fair election. If they fail, the public will lose confidence in future local elections and other elections held under party-led governments, and people will lose interest in elections,” he said.
Thakurgaon Superintendent of Police Belal Hossain said voting began peacefully at all 185 polling centers at 8am.
He said all centers were being monitored through online body-worn cameras and equipped with CCTV cameras, adding that polling had proceeded peacefully across the constituency.

item.title: Gas emerges from submersible pump in Gopalganj, ignites into flames
item.description:
Gas emerging from a submersible pump in Gopalganj’s Kotalipara upazila has caught fire when exposed to a lighter, prompting locals to call for an expert investigation.
The incident occurred at Bhashai Bazar in Bandhabari union, where hardware trader Kamrul Sheikh installed the pump about a year ago to supply water to fish transport vehicles.
Kamrul said the pump had been producing less water over the past week. Out of curiosity, he held a gas lighter near the pipe’s opening on Wednesday night, and flames erupted.
News of the incident quickly spread, drawing crowds to his shop on Thursday. At the request of curious onlookers, Kamrul repeatedly demonstrated how the gas caught fire when a lighter was brought near the pipe.
The residents urged the authorities to send a team of experts to determine whether natural gas was present underground.
Kamrul, son of Rob Sheikh, said he had installed the pump at a depth of 280 feet to supply water to fish transport vehicles.
Local youth Shihab Sheikh said he visited the site on Thursday morning after hearing about the incident the previous night.
“We witnessed the phenomenon ourselves. We want a team of experts to examine the site and determine whether there is really gas underground. If gas is found here, it could benefit the country,” he said.
Kotalipara Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Saif-ul-Arefin said he had sent local land officials to the site after learning about the incident.
“Based on their initial report, I have received confirmation of the incident. I will visit the site on Friday and decide on the next steps,” he said.

item.title: Dr Zahed: Youth should help seniors identify fake news
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting and Cultural Affairs Adviser Dr Zahed Ur Rahman has urged young people to help senior citizens develop media and information literacy skills to identify fake news and misinformation.
He made the call as the chief guest at a seminar titled “Media and Information Literacy Skills for 21st Century Youth” and a special award ceremony at the Manzur Elahi Auditorium of East West University (EWU) on October 29, 2026.
Addressing the gathering, Zahed said fake news and misinformation were spreading rapidly in Bangladesh, as in the rest of the world. He said the government prioritized educating and empowering citizens over imposing strict regulatory controls.
He also noted that older adults were often more vulnerable to misinformation on social media than younger people, urging the youth to help seniors identify inauthentic information.
The event was organized by EWU's Department of Information Studies as part of the nationwide celebration of Global Media and Information Literacy (MIL) Week 2026. It was held in collaboration with the UNESCO Dhaka Office, the Media and Information Literacy Network Bangladesh (MILNetBD), and the UN Electoral Project “Ballot.”
Professor Dr Mohammed Farashuddin, chairperson of EWU's Board of Trustees, chaired the seminar.
Professor Dr M Ashik Mosaddik, acting vice-chancellor of EWU; Dr Susan Vize, UNESCO representative to Bangladesh; and Andrés del Castillo Sánchez, representative of the UN Electoral Project “Ballot” Bangladesh, attended as special guests.
Professor Dr Dilara Begum, chairperson of EWU's Department of Information Studies, presented the keynote paper, which was discussed by Professor Dr Kazi Mostak Gausul Hoq of the Department of Information Science and Library Management at the University of Dhaka.
Following the seminar, awards were presented to students and awareness advocates in recognition of their contributions to the week-long media literacy activities.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,249 as seven die in 24 hours
item.description:
Seven more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Thursday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,249.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all seven of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,144, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 105, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the seven new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with four deaths.
A total of 1,251 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Thursday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 226,357.
During the same period, 64 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 23,695.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 201,468 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 193,301 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Five of a family burned in Gazipur gas leak fire
item.description:
Five members of a family suffered burn injuries in a fire caused by a gas leak in Kashimpur, Gazipur, on Thursday morning.
The victims were taken to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka for treatment around 2pm.
The fire broke out in the Sardagong area of Kashimpur at around 8:30am on Thursday.
The injured were identified as Arifa Begum, Faria, Rozina, 18, child Rahim and Riazul Sheikh.
Riazul suffered burns to 40% of his body, while Arifa sustained burns to 5%, Faria to 8%, and Rozina and one-year-old Rahim to less than 1% each. Riazul's condition is critical.
Talha Bin Jasim, an official at the Fire Service and Civil Defence media cell, said, quoting Dr Sultan Mahmud Shikder, resident surgeon (emergency) at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery, that all five victims were receiving necessary treatment and remained under observation.
